# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired really easily, more so than other kids his age, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Feeding has been a challenge, with the patient having trouble eating certain foods and sometimes showing discomfort after meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than expected and has subtle differences in movement when playing or doing physical tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and intellectual disability.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to have inconsistent hearing, sometimes responding to sounds and other times not, and has required multiple ear infections and possible hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, which can make things tricky for him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth, which can make biting and chewing harder.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school and may require special education plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has subtle differences in movement and falls more often than expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves around differently than his peers, with subtle but noticeable differences in physical tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate potential heart conditions
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address challenges
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess potential skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue and tires easily, especially during physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences occasional bowel problems that can be frustrating and disrupt daily routines.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower in reaching certain milestones as a baby, such as walking or sitting up, and needed more time and support than other kids his age to master these skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the TV volume way up to hear his favorite shows clearly, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple aeration tube insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things that are far away and often squints or gets closer to see better, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip really easily, even with minor accidents, affecting his confidence in eating and smiling.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues are affecting his schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or remaining in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or other interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture when standing or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any issues promptly.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate and treat any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess heart health.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to evaluate bone health and structure.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support development and address specific challenges.

Parent: Our son often squints when trying to focus on things, which makes us worry about his eyesight. It's not just when reading or watching TV; it happens even when he's playing or looking at pictures.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that requires regular check-ups to monitor it closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, including trouble latching on and getting frustrated easily, but this phase has passed, and he now eats fairly normally.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which can be managed with medication, and has scoliosis that affects his posture and can cause back pain if not managed properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, and some may have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to have hearing difficulties, picking up on some sounds but completely missing others, and has required regular hearing reviews.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on things, which makes his parents worry about his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are very prone to breaking or chipping, and he has to be careful with what he eats and make sure he brushes them gently but thoroughly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to express himself clearly and has difficulty finding the right words or explaining what he wants or needs, for which he is receiving speech therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, although some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and behavioural differences, including difficulty with speech and expression.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis that affects his posture and can cause back pain if not managed properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent decay or damage.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and adjust treatment as needed.
* Neurological review to monitor the patient's seizures and adjust medication as needed.
* Speech therapy to help the patient improve his communication skills.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioural concerns.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if the patient's height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart, which requires monitoring. This hasn't limited his physical activity, but his parents keep a close eye on how he's doing, especially after exertion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movements challenges, including constipation or loose stools, which can be uncomfortable and worrisome for both him and his parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and gastrointestinal issues are common in people with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was diagnosed with hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, making him feel stiffer than other kids his age. He needs to work on exercises to help improve this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome may experience developmental delay, seizures, and other neurological issues, with around 20-40% of people reported to have seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing, especially in noisy environments, and has had instances where he doesn't respond immediately to his name being called.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in class, squints when watching TV or trying to read, and has been commented on by his teacher for having difficulty copying from the board.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist more often than usual due to various issues such as cavities and weak tooth structure, leading to several fillings and discussions about preventive measures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia and scoliosis, which require regular check-ups and interventions to ensure proper development and prevent future complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to monitor vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor bone health and development
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise
* Regular check-ups to monitor hip dysplasia and scoliosis and prevent future complications

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing or running around, which may be related to overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing or running around, which may be related to overall development and requires monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Feeding was tricky when the patient was a baby; she didn't take to bottle feeding easily and would spit up often. However, now she eats well and doesn't complain about tummy aches.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which is low muscle tone compared to other kids her age. Physical therapy has helped a lot. The patient also experiences speech delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear when she was younger, but after treatment, it cleared up nicely. Now she can hear just fine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to squint a lot, which can make her eyes look a bit crossed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Cold foods and drinks seem to bother the patient's teeth quite a bit; she complains they feel sensitive.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important. Regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences speech delays and may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delays and hypotonia, which may impact her development and behavior.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than usual, which might be related to some genetic factor.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for any changes in hearing
* Eyesight review to assess for any vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor for any heart conditions
* Physical therapy to continue supporting the patient's hypotonia
* Speech therapy to support the patient's speech development
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily, especially when playing with friends, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be picky about eating certain foods, with some textures or smells putting her off completely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes stares off into space for a few seconds, like she's in a trance, and has delayed speech compared to other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear last year and needed antibiotics to clear it up, and her hearing seems fine now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means she needs glasses to see clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Cold foods and drinks make her teeth hurt sometimes, and the patient has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech is delayed compared to other kids her age, and she doesn't talk as much as you'd expect.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech and stares off into space for a few seconds, like she's in a trance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may experience developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Speech therapy to address delayed speech
* Behavioral therapy to address staring spells and potential anxiety or ADHD
* Regular monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address any delays or difficulties.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's heart rate can get pretty high when he's playing or running around, though not dangerously so. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble with feeding as a baby, including latching on and spitting up, and still deals with occasional constipation issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily when physically active and has speech development issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has some difficulty hearing certain sounds or frequencies, particularly in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and uses glasses to correct this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go to the dentist more often than most kids his age due to tooth decay and sensitivity issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development is delayed, and he is working on exercises at home to encourage more talk.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech development issues and may have other behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth decay and sensitivity issues
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart conditions
* Speech therapy to address speech development issues
* Occupational therapy to address any fine motor skill delays
* Behavioral therapy to address any behavioral differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if necessary
* Consideration of physiotherapy to address any gross motor skill delays

a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV up to very high levels, indicating a potential issue with her hearing.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit extremely close to the television or when reading books, raising concerns about her eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip rather easily, requiring frequent dental visits.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor and manage hearing concerns
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor and manage vision concerns
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor and manage heart condition
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor and manage skeletal concerns

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular check-ups to monitor her heart health, and the cardiologist is managing her condition to prevent any complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be quite picky about what she eats, which can make mealtime tricky, but otherwise, her digestion seems okay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome, and some may require short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and requires medication management to control her condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hearing difficulties, with times when she seems to pick up on some sounds perfectly fine but then misses others, and has required medical attention for her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurry vision, which may be related to her glasses or another factor, and requires further evaluation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods and drinks, which may be due to the formation of her teeth or decay, and requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have weak enamel, large front teeth, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and requires support in her educational journey, with discussions ongoing with her therapists and doctors to understand better and find ways to support her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, is not talking as much as expected for her age, and has required more time to reach milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy to manage these conditions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and decay
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to assess hearing difficulties
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate blurry vision
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consideration of a palate review, particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess skeletal anomalies
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences
* Regular check-ups with the cardiologist to monitor heart health
* Management of epilepsy with medication and lifestyle adjustments
* Support for educational and developmental needs, including potential special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart condition that has been mentioned during check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is quite picky about food and often refuses to try new things, making mealtime a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has seizures sometimes, which can be scary to watch.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond right away when called, possibly due to hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things that are far away, such as the board in her classroom, affecting her performance at school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip really easily, requiring careful brushing and a restricted diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision problems are affecting her performance at school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia that is being monitored by doctors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage or chipping.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing difficulties.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone health and detect potential skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and difficulties.
* Regular monitoring of hip dysplasia and adjustment of treatment as necessary.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, with varying types and responses to treatment, and some may have tethered cord, leading to pain, weakness, and urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient turns the volume of the TV up really high to hear it properly, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV when watching shows or reads books, potentially indicating vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods, and avoids those foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, requiring regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's communication difficulties lead to frustration when expressing herself clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school and some requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans, due to developmental delay and learning difficulties.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues and communication difficulties, leading to frustration.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems and potential need for glasses or surgery
* Cardiac review to monitor heart abnormality and potential need for treatment
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address coordination, communication, and developmental issues
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in his heart, which is being monitored through regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble eating and digesting food, making mealtimes a daily struggle.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to start walking and sitting compared to other babies, indicating developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing certain sounds and sometimes doesn't respond to his name being called, indicating potential hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints sometimes, especially when looking at things closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth that stick out more than other kids' teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have weak enamel and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has short fingers and hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal development
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and behavioural differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in his heart, which is being monitored through regular check-ups to ensure it does not significantly impact his daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gains weight slowly compared to his peers, although he eats well and does not show signs of discomfort after eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a tethered cord, which could potentially affect his development, and he has scoliosis, for which he is undergoing physical therapy to improve his posture and reduce the curvature of his spine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological developmental delays. Tethered cord has been found in about 11% of children with KBG syndrome, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has times when he doesn't respond right away to his name being called, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple grommet insertions and some needing hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit very close to the TV or leans in close when looking at pictures, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Regular eyesight reviews are recommended.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been complaining about tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods, which started a few months ago and has been consistent since then.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which requires careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or remaining in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis and is undergoing physical therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and may have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and overall dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to assess and address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to check for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Continued monitoring of the heart condition by a cardiologist.
* Physical therapy to manage scoliosis and improve posture.
* Consideration of referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal abnormalities.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is managed with diet adjustments and occasional medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out quicker than her peers during physical activities, which has been noticeable since she started school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises and gets frustrated in crowded or noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, which has been an ongoing issue and may affect her schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires more frequent dental check-ups due to various issues, including cavities and sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's blurry vision may affect her schoolwork.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental issues

* Cardiac review to monitor the structural abnormality in the heart

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes seems to hear just fine, but other times doesn't respond even when spoken to directly, indicating possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means she has trouble seeing things clearly unless they're really close up.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are very prone to breaking or chipping, requiring careful management of diet and eating habits.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage or chipping.

* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and manage symptoms.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily and has a short playtime before needing to rest, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation and requires a diet rich in water and fruits to help alleviate this issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, which is managed with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear in the past, which seems to have improved, and currently experiences squinting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints when looking at things, indicating a potential vision problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break easily, requiring careful management of their diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups crucial.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient talks late and seems behind other kids in learning skills such as buttoning shirts and using the potty.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and is behind in acquiring skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent further breakage.
* Regular hearing reviews to ensure no recurrence of glue ear and to address any hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess and correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review to investigate and manage any potential heart conditions.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.
* Management of epilepsy with medication and regular neurological check-ups.
* Dietary management to help with constipation.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart with an unspecified abnormality, which may require surgery or monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constant diarrhea and bowel movement challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord, which may cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear, which has since cleared up, and experiences hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, squints, and trouble seeing things far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel and requires careful dental care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects their back.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor scoliosis and other skeletal issues
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble going to the bathroom regularly, with constipation being a big issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may experience feeding difficulties, and a proportion have subtle anomalies of the palate, which can affect speech development and feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's muscles seem too weak sometimes, diagnosed as hypotonia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks to have things repeated because he didn't catch them the first time, suggesting hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things look blurry sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Cold foods and drinks make his teeth hurt, and he was born with shorter fingers than usual, which can make some tasks tricky for him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with shorter fingers than usual.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any issues promptly.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and manage any hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct any vision problems.
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess heart health.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular check-ups for signs of tethered cord, especially if sacral dimple is present.

Parent: One thing that's caught our attention is how easily he gets tired compared to his peers. a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to struggle with hearing certain sounds, despite normal hearing tests.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs his eyes when trying to focus, especially during screen time or reading, suggesting potential vision problems.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness quickly when engaging in physical activities, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiac issues, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, are reported in approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has sensory issues and certain food textures make him uncomfortable, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epilepsy and has to take medication regularly to manage his seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media in the past, a recurring issue that has affected his hearing, and he often squints or leans forward to get a better view, indicating possible vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint are common.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in class and often squints or leans forward to get a better view.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are not strong; they break or chip easily, requiring several trips to the dentist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and is behind his peers in terms of development, requiring therapy sessions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delay and speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers are common.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to address vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for cardiac issues.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to address developmental delays and behavioural differences.
* Regular monitoring and management of epilepsy and seizures.
* Consider referral for a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular check-ups to monitor her heart health, with a cardiologist stating that so far, everything has been stable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, is quite picky about what she eats, and some foods she just won't touch, even if they're her favorites sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a lack of interest in feeding being significant and long-lasting in some cases.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, with weaker muscles than expected for her age, and is working with a physiotherapist to help strengthen them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear recently, which was due to a buildup of fluid, and was given medication to clear it up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things look blurry sometimes, which has been happening for a while now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint, with treatment including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods like meat or carrots, and manages softer foods okay, but meal times have been adjusted to ensure she can eat comfortably.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, with careful brushing being very important, and regular dental check-ups being recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not speaking as much as expected for her age, and when she tries to communicate, it can be hard to understand what she means, with speech therapy being considered to help.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most going to a mainstream primary school, but some transferring to special schooling or remaining in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication being appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), with babies experiencing a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head, and many having short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess the patient's vision.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the patient's heart health.
* Consider a palate review, particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
* Speech therapy to help the patient with communication.
* Physiotherapy to help strengthen the patient's muscles.
* Occupational therapy to help the patient with fine motor skills.
* Behavioural therapy to help the patient with any behavioural difficulties.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits a strong aversion to certain textures and tastes, making mealtime stressful.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord, which could potentially cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks for repetitions of what was just said, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit close to the TV and holds books close to her face, suggesting potential vision issues, and has complained about tooth sensitivity which might be related to overall sensory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, especially with cold foods.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
